title: THE PROPHET MICAIAH
mv: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, by whom we may enquire of the LORD: but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.
mvp: ‘‘And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, by whom we may enquire of the LORD: but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.’’ 1 Kings 22:8
assignment: Are you in a situation that demands you choose between standing for what is right or compromise, to avoid being labelled as ‘Too Righteous’? Choose to stand for what is right (No mark).

b.x: Micaiah, in Hebrew, means, “Who is like Yahweh.’’ The son of Imlah, he was a fearless prophet during the reign of King Ahab. Micaiah was known for his accurate prophecies. For instance, he predicted the defeat and death of King Ahab in his battle with the Syrians, and so it was. He is featured explicitly in the Books of 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles. He is one of the four disciples of Elijah who stood out in his prophecy against 400 unanimous prophets of doom who persuaded King Ahab to go to battle.

A major character trait of the prophet, Micaiah, is truthfulness. He distinguished himself from the 400 prophets who gave the king a false prophecy by his tenacity in sticking to the truth even though it was not popular (2 Chronicles 18:12-13). He was a man of integrity; he remained upright even as fake prophets mill around the king with their deceitful predictions (1 Kings 22:6-8). He had a track record of hearing from God expressly and delivering that same message (1Kings 22:14). He never wavered in his trust in God. Even when he was informed that he would be thrown into the dungeon, he held on to his belief in the God of Israel (1 Kings 22:26-28).

i: Daring: Micaiah was courageous enough to let King Ahab know that the 400 prophets speaking in his favour were filled with a lying spirit from the Lord and that evil would befall him in the battle with the Syrians (1 Kings 22:19-23).

Independent: He stood alone in his conviction and prophecy to the king without shifting ground (1 Kings 22:27-28). As individuals, we may sometimes have to stand alone for our beliefs in the truth of God’s word.

Sought After: He was in demand because of the power of God in his life. King Ahab had to send an officer to bring him when Jehoshaphat insisted that a prophet of the Lord should be sought for a word from God (1 Kings 22:5-7; 9).

Clarity: He was precise and did not mince words in his response to the King’s question on his safe return. He simply declared to him that he would not return to Israel (1 Kings 22:28). This is because he had heard expressly from God.

Focus: Despite the persuasion by the King’s officer to convince Micaiah to follow the pattern of the prevalent lies by the 400 prophets in Israel, he was insistent and single-minded to declare only the counsel of the Lord (2 Chronicles 18:12-13).
Faithful: He was humiliated for speaking the truth by one of the false prophets, but he remained faithful and offered His service to God even in the face of opposition (2 Chronicles 18:23-24).
Confidence: Although 400 false prophets said the same thing, Micaiah refused to be swayed; rather, he remained unyielding and sure of the prophecy God gave through him (2 Chronicles 18:27).

b.x: We must stand for the truth and be resolute to do what is right, even in the face of opposition.

i: Briefly describe Prophet Micaiah in your own words.
State four qualities from his life.
